title: I Used the Bus-Terminal Locker Timer After They Held My Bay Overnight

parts.text: I paid locker C9 until 6:00 p.m. and at 6:11 the LED still showed OCCUPIED under a staff override. The sticker said: TIMER ENDS. STAFF CLEARS. NO OVERNIGHT HOLDS. Clerk Vince had a suitcase tag on C9 that was not mine. I was twenty-eight, traveler, holding a receipt. "Overrides are the bay." I photographed the LED, the receipt, and the tag. Then I logged a hold. At 6:18 the terminal lead asked why Vince's override was on a paid-out locker. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The terminal lead can see Vince's staff override on C9 after my 6:00 timer.

social.video_title: Staff overrode my locker after the timer ended — Part 1/2
social.description: Bus terminal, a paid-out locker, and a staff LED. I logged the hold. Would you have photographed the tag?

parts.text: Vince called it lost-and-found until the lead asked for the log. I printed the hold, the photo, and the sticker. C9 opened. Vince found luggage in the actual lost cage and told clerks found was always about optics. Optics is a word overrides use when a tag exists. Timer policy now has a second line: OVERRIDES ARE NOT OVERNIGHT. I keep the receipt. Vince cages. The bay finally looks like a locker, not a closet. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.description: Hold log, opened locker, and a second line. Was lost-and-found ever C9?
